title: A second-pulse constraint added nine efficiency failures in 103 selected Allen input models at correlation cap 0.5
abstract: We tested whether a fixed positive readout can keep high efficiency for first, second and late 50 Hz response summaries in Allen cortical slices. At an assumed absolute noise correlation cap of 0.5, the best fixed readout fell below 80 percent efficiency in 16 of 103 selected input groups. A matched first-and-late test had seven failures. Adding the second response thus added nine failures. Under independent noise, the counts were four and one. Efficiency is a ratio of robust squared signal-to-noise values, not a guarantee against an optimum that knows the actual covariance. Independent global upper checks passed within 1e-6. Stored medians were assigned as means. Unknown covariance, fit uncertainty, different temporal averaging, selected slices and absent held-out trials prevent a neuronal decoding claim. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Matched two-summary and three-summary fixed-readout efficiencies. Correlation caps and the 80 percent rule are assumptions. Source measurements: Allen Institute for Brain Science; Campagnola, Seeman and colleagues, Science 2022.
